title: William VIII, Lord of Montpellier
summary: This document provides biographical information about William VIII, Lord of Montpellier (died 1202), son of William VII and Matilda of Burgundy. The main points covered include: his first marriage to Eudokia Komnene, grand-niece of Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos, which produced one daughter, Marie of Montpellier; his separation from Eudokia (whom he sent to a monastery) due to lacking a male heir, followed by his marriage to Agnes of Castile, with whom he had eight children—all of whom are listed by name along with details of their marriages or religious vocations; the Pope's ruling that his marriage to Agnes was illegitimate, resulting in Marie inheriting the lordship; and his role as a patron of troubadours, particularly Arnaut de Mareuil, who fled to his court and addressed at least one poem to him.
